stage1.impression: A long, warm view from the street into a deep timber room: a lit counter with low pendants, a record wall on the left, a pair of speakers far away under hazy spots, and a dark, grimy steel shopfront framing it all. The depth and the pools of light work, and the far end is moody. But it reads as a competent CG render, not a photograph. The window has no glass in it: no reflections, no etched name. The ceiling timber tiles in every bay. A clipped white disc floats in the middle of the frame like a moon. The steel's grunge looks like a stretched decal. The speakers are 40-50 px grey boxes that nobody would spot as the hero. As it stands, a magazine would see a generic dark bar seen through a hole, not a specific place.

blocking_9: The shopfront must read as glass: visible street reflections and the etched name legible on the pane over the room
The frosted lightbox with the dancing woman's fogged silhouette must be in frame and read at a glance; it is not visible (the frosted panel at 940-980,205-415 glows evenly, with no figure)
No clipped floating point source mid-frame (region 640-665,225-250 is 57.6 % clipped)
The ceiling timber must not tile: each bay between 300-770,60-300 now shows the same blotch pattern
The blackened steel's patina must read as real oxidised steel at 1:1, not a high-contrast grunge decal (770-870,0-800 and the lintel 870-1120,120-210)
The altar pair must be found by the eye within a second: larger in frame or set off by a clearer light contrast against the wainscot behind
A sign of life near the glass (a figure at the counter, or a coat or glass close to the window), so the room reads as open and lived in, not as a set

defects.what: A pure white clipped disc floating in front of the back wall: 57.6 % clipped, reads as a bare bulb or moon, not as a warm #FFD2A0 disc
The shopfront glass is invisible: no reflection, no etched name (the etched name's glow is 0.0), so the window reads as an open hole
The ceiling timber repeats the same mottled texture in every bay
The steel column's patina is blotchy white flecks over near-black, like a stretched grunge map; no sharp edge sheen
The lintel and the right-hand facade panels carry the same grunge decal, with flat tile-like panels
The frosted panel is an even rectangle with no silhouette; if this is the lightbox, the dancing figure does not read
The corrugated column has a smooth CG vertical gradient and specular streak and reads as plastic
The speakers are tiny and grey (smoked tint plus white batts) against a brown wainscot; the haze cones above them draw more attention than the cabinets
The foreground sill is 14.7 % crushed, median 11.6: a dead black band
The floor is wet-glossy with smeared reflections, slightly denoiser-soft
The grade is orange-brown overall (r 41 / g 28 / b 22 median); the concrete reads tan rather than warm grey

out_of_scope.request: Give the hero speakers a visible saturated tint so they carry the frame's one colour
out_of_scope.why: The Smoke configuration fixes the speakers' tint; in Smoke the frame has no saturated accent by design. Light and camera are the only levers (c6, c2).

out_of_scope.request: Replace the corrugated column at 980-1080,205-515 with a better-reading material
out_of_scope.why: It is part of the shopfront's design; only its finish (roughness, sheen variation) may change
